events.title: Hubble gets corrective optics
events.description: Astronauts service the space telescope to improve its images.

events.title: South Africa holds a democratic election
events.description: The country holds its first national democratic election open to all races.

events.title: Windows 95 reaches stores
events.description: Microsoft launches a new operating system with a Start menu and taskbar.

what_happened_next.text:
Honda nearly tripled in dollar terms, leading these choices. The US share basket more than doubled, while Hasbro and IBM also gained. A broad international basket gained less than this particular Japanese company. One company cannot stand in for a whole country or tell you how all foreign shares will behave.

The world beyond markets also changed. Astronauts repaired Hubble in 1993. South Africa held a national democratic election open to all races in 1994. Microsoft launched Windows 95 in 1995, bringing its Start menu to many computer users.

None of those events was a ready-made answer to the investment question. Knowing a technology would matter did not automatically reveal which company's shares would deliver the largest gain, or what price was sensible to pay.

Look at the months between the start and finish. Would a fall have made you want to change your mind? Your choice was made without this chart. The comparison is useful because it shows the gap between what sounded plausible at the time and the particular path that eventually occurred.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: People followed the Winter Olympics, new technology, car prices and efforts to protect the ozone layer.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The full monthly paths, including sharp falls, mattered more than any one product announcement. The US-traded Honda share is measured in dollars, so its result is not a local-currency Japanese market return.
reflection.what_faded_away: The Toy Fair’s most surprising designs did not reveal which investment would finish first. Olympic results were no investing shortcut either.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Honda’s later lead was unknown. Higher car prices could have different effects on customers, sales and company profits.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: Honda found new buyers with vehicles built for families and recreation. It launched the Odyssey minivan in Japan in October 1994 and the CR-V in 1995. These models helped revive its Japanese business during a difficult period. The investment rose strongly while Honda’s product range expanded beyond its familiar cars.

Hasbro’s games and toys brought in more money. Its 1996 sales passed $3 billion, up 5%, and profit was about $200 million. Board games, computer versions of games and Star Wars toys helped. Those results, reported in February 1997, show concrete business progress during the investment’s five-year rise.

IBM’s deep losses gave way to about $3 billion of profit in 1994 and $4.2 billion in 1995. Services revenue grew, and the July 1995 Lotus acquisition added business software. The investment finished higher as the company rebuilt its earnings. This window includes a painful decline before that recovery took hold.
